lines.text: Ilse reached the gallery. Three hundred years of the Order's records stood there on wooden shelves, dry as old bread.
She opened Tobin's lantern, took out its burning heart of rimeglass, and pushed it into the oldest ledgers she could find.
I've wanted to do this for even longer than the seal.
The shelves went up like kindling. Burning pages came floating down through the dark like snow, and landed on the Heartstone.
The Stone screamed. I don't know another word for it. The blue light in its veins flared white, and the woman in the cage cried out.
And Vance looked away from us.
The moment his eyes left them, every thread I had came back to life at once. Wren gasped. Oswin's sword finished its swing. Ash landed, snarling, on nothing at all.
If the Stone burns, she burns with it. And whatever it's holding lets go. He knows it. Look at his face!
I looked. For the first time since I had known him, the Grand Measurer was afraid.
Open the sluices! All of them! Bring the ice! Caddoc, the Stone! Now!
Somewhere above us, gates groaned open, and cold water came roaring down into the vault. The Lowmarket's water. The water he had stolen for twenty years, to keep his Stone cold.
He chose the Stone. I watched him choose it. He let us go to save it.
And water that pours in has to pour out. I saw the drain at once, a black arch at the far side of the vault, where the stolen water ran away.
There! Under the arch! Go!
The others ran. I couldn't. Not yet. I went back to the bars.
I'll come back for you. I swear it. Do you hear me? I'll come back.
I'll be here.
She said it as if it were a joke. Fifteen winters, chained to a stone. Of course she would be here.
Wren dragged me away. Fire was falling all around the Heartstone, and the water was rising past my knees.
Behind us, I heard Vance give one more order, very calmly, as if nothing at all had happened.
Caddoc. After them.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and eight, coming soon.
